items.originalTitle: Mexico wants a say in where SpaceX flies — says harmful rocket debris keeps washing up on its shores
items.originalSummary: Mexican authorities say SpaceX must take responsibility for suspected rocket debris washing up on a beach near the Texas border, after a Starship booster exploded over the Gulf of Mexico last week. The fragments began arriving Tuesday at Bagdad Beach near Matamoros in Tamaulipas, south of SpaceX's Starbase launch site in Texas. Environmental group Conibio Global says it has found at least 1,500 fragments . The group's president, Jesús Elías Ibarra, says there are thousands. The pieces include plastic, rubber and adhesive the group believes came from the booster, though it says the origin still needs confirming. Mexico's National Commission of Natural Protected Areas and Conibio are collecting the debris . The booster exploded during the Nov.13 test flight after an aborted catch attempt because the engines stopped firing too soon. The company’s expansion has affected dozens of U.S. citizens in the surrounding area who claim these launches have had direct effects on their households. Mexico's environmental protection agency, Profepa urged the public not to touch fragments and to report them. A Caguama turtle was found dead and environmental groups are making an autopsy to determine whether the debris’ potentially toxic materials were the cause of death. Debris from another SpaceX explosion reached the Tamaulipas coast last year, too. President Claudia Sheinbaum threatened legal action, but in July she ruled out a lawsuit for now, saying Mexico would pursue talks with the U.S. instead. SpaceX said then that tests of materials inside Starship found no chemical, biological or toxicological risks, and that it wanted to work with Mexico to recover the debris. The debris adds to a wider fight over SpaceX's Texas expansion. A federal judge in September refused to block a land swap giving SpaceX 715 acres of wildlife refuge, which environmental groups had sued over. In August, Brownsville agreed to remove 444 acres from city limits in exchange for up to $220 million for water projects. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa asked Texas Parks and Wildlife to take no action on a possible Boca Chica State Park land sale to SpaceX during her transition. People on both sides of the border are taking the hit of Space X’s expansion. Prices have skyrocketed, and environmentalists claim the toxicity will affect the fauna of the region.

items.originalTitle: Citigroup raises Nebius Group price target to $324, maintains Buy
items.originalSummary: Nebius Group (NBIS) was hit by a sharp repricing after Reuters reported on November 12, 2026 that the company cut its 2026 revenue forecast because of delays in third-party capacity additions. Reuters said the stock fell 16% that day as investors reacted to the slowdown risk in US data-center buildout, even as Nebius raised annual spending guidance and said it expects to rely more on customer prepayments and asset-backed financing. That is the core issue here: the market is no longer only rewarding growth; it is forcing Nebius to prove it can keep capacity online fast enough to support the revenue ramp. The latest market snapshot shows NBIS at $82.69, down 14.21% over 24 hours, with a session range of $96.56 to $81.74. Volume was $226.7 million on Binance futures, which is high enough to confirm strong interest, but not necessarily healthy demand. The chart structure is plainly bearish. NBIS is below its 7-day SMA of $89.22, 20-day SMA of $112.55, and 50-day SMA of $150.04, with the moving averages stacked in bearish alignment. The 12-day EMA at $99.27 and 26-day EMA at $118.18 reinforce that the trend remains oversold relative to the recent base.

items.originalTitle: China's 'StarCompute' 32-PFLOPS Satellite Completes 45-Minute In-Orbit Training, Surpassing Google's 15 Minutes
items.originalSummary: Adaspace said on November 25, 2026 that its eight-satellite Star Compute Group 02 constellation completed 45 minutes and 33 seconds of continuous full-parameter AI training during a single orbit, citing the first third-party in-orbit capability test data from the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology. The academy is a research institution under China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. Its data covers in-orbit training and inference-service validation using Alibaba’s Qwen3-32B model. The announcement puts one Group 02 satellite’s nominal capacity at 32 PFLOPS, a unit representing one quadrillion floating-point operations per second, using FP8 precision, an 8-bit format for AI training and inference. Adaspace described the results as initial evidence that its technical approach is feasible and as engineering data for future space-computing development. Training loss, defined as the model’s average error on the data it is learning, steadily declined. Forward propagation, backward propagation, gradient calculation and weight updates were all completed in orbit. Those steps cover the closed loop that updates model parameters, so the test went beyond inference alone. The constellation also validated inference services, but the continuous run documents that the training process itself could be executed onboard. A separate test covered the thermal system needed for high-power payloads. The announcement says Adaspace’s 10-kilowatt-class liquid-cooling fluid-loop system and extra-large deployable radiative cooling wings operated normally and met the thermal-control requirements for continuous computing-payload operation at that power level, supporting long-term stable operation of high-performance computing satellites. Citing public information, Adaspace said Google’s in-orbit prototype satellite using a tensor processing unit, or TPU , has a maximum single-run duration of about 15 minutes. Group 02 therefore exceeded the Google satellite’s continuous in-orbit training duration, according to the company’s comparison. That comparison concerns duration only; it does not establish a broader performance ranking between the systems. The eight Group 02 satellites were successfully launched from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on October 14, 2026. Adaspace reports that their deployment raised Star Compute’s total capacity to approximately 50 POPS, with POPS representing one quadrillion operations per second, and describes the network as the world’s largest computing constellation currently in orbit. Group 02 is Adaspace’s second AI computing constellation, following the 12-satellite system developed and launched on May 14, 2025. The company’s November 5, 2026 prospectus describes AI computing satellites as using onboard computing resources and algorithms to provide data analysis and computing services for their own operations, other spacecraft and ground applications. The prospectus set out four Group 02 validation goals: high-power liquid cooling, large deployable radiative wings, an all-domain laser communications network and in-orbit training of AI foundation models. historyItems.originalTitle: Analog Devices Q4 FY 2026: Optical Demand Drives Data Center Growth
historyItems.originalSummary: Analog Devices, Inc. ADI reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of $4.06 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.4%. The bottom line increased 80% year over year. Revenues of $4.37 billion surpassed the consensus mark by 1.2% and increased 42% year over year. The strong performance was driven by sustained demand across industrial and data center markets, alongside a broader cyclical recovery. historyItems.originalTitle: Boeing Wins $7.4 Billion Order in Biggest China Buy in Years
historyItems.originalSummary: Boeing ( BA , Financials ) on landed a deal to sell 50 Boeing 737-8 jets to China Southern Airlines' Xiamen Airlines for a total list price of around $7.4 billion.China Southern reported the deal in a stock exchange filing, saying the effective acquisition price would be lower because Boeing gave a large reduction.Deliveries of the aircraft are expected to be in stages from 2031 to 2034, pending clearance from shareholders and the Chinese government.The deal followed a pledge by China to buy 200 planes at a summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in May. But the filing did not say whether the latest order was part of that pledge.Trump stated China would order another 250 Boeing planes but Chinese authorities have not confirmed any more orders.China Southern said the purchase will help Xiamen Airlines strengthen its fleet and expand at the new Xiamen Xiang'an International Airport.The deal comes as Boeing looks to repair its reputation in China after nearly a decade without a big order from the country.Investors will be looking for regulatory approvals and possibly more orders for planes from Chinese carriers.

historyItems.originalTitle: 49ers and Meta Announce Multi-Year Partnership Centered Around Meta AI Glasses
historyItems.originalSummary: The San Francisco 49ers and Meta today announced a landmark multi-year partnership, naming Meta the Official Moment Maker of the NFL franchise. Built on a shared commitment to innovate and create meaningful memories for life, the partnership unites two Bay Area-born organizations for the future of the sports fan experience. Headlining the partnership, the 49ers and Meta plan to gift all 49ers suite partners and club season ticket members a free pair of Oakley Meta HSTN AI glasses to celebrate the 49ers 80th anniversary. Through this initiative, more than 4,700 members will receive Meta’s next-gen technology directly to their homes, giving them a first-of-its-kind VIP experience. Oakley Meta HSTN AI glasses allow fans to capture their fan experience through photos and videos hands-free, listen to music, and get help from Meta AI, all while staying in the moment “Innovation and technology are part of our franchise’s DNA, from the West Coast offense, to Levi’s® Stadium, to the future of the fan experience,” said Brent Schoeb, 49ers Chief Operating Officer. “Meta has been at the forefront of technology for a long time. That, paired with being Silicon Valley neighbors, made this partnership a perfect fit. We are thrilled to continue providing members with exclusive benefits and look forward to seeing the content they create with Meta’s AI glasses.” In addition to gifting thousands of Meta AI glasses, Meta has joined the 49ers global marketing efforts in the UK, UAE, and Mexico as part of the NFL’s Global Markets Program. Over the next several years, Meta will support the team’s mission to reach new fans, grow the game of American football, and leave a lasting impact on international communities. As a first step, WhatsApp, owned by Meta, has been named the Official Instant Messenger Provider of the 49ers, enabling fast and efficient communication globally for the team. “Game day is about being in the moment from the tailgate to victory and the best way to capture it all is handsfree with Oakley Meta glasses. As a lifelong member of the 49ers Faithful, I’m fired up that we are now an official partner and will help connect fans to the team we love,” said Andrew Bosworth, Chief Technology Officer at Meta. Meta and the 49ers plan to explore additional opportunities to integrate technology and AI across the organization. This season, 49ers fans can also look forward to seeing 49ers FB Kyle Juszczyk sport Meta AI glasses as a brand ambassador in a new campaign. For more information, please visit 49ers.com.

Despite the reaffirmed outlook and new deals, AST SpaceMobile's share price has been under pressure, with a 7 day share price return of down 25.94% and a 30 day share price return of down 37.88% as investors weigh dilution, launch risk, and heavy spend on the Blacklift rocket. The 1 year total shareholder return is down 49.61%, but the 3 year total shareholder return is still up by a very large multiple, suggesting momentum has faded in the near term even while early backers remain well ahead overall.

historyItems.originalTitle: Live coverage: SpaceX to launch classified payload for the U.S. Space Force
historyItems.originalSummary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stands at Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base ahead of the launch of the NROL-179 mission. Image: SpaceX A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket is being readied to send a classified payload to orbit Tuesday morning from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on behalf of the U.S. Space Force. The USSF-266 mission will be the fifth government mission launched by SpaceX this month, four for the Space Force and one for the National Reconnaissance Office. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 4 East is scheduled during a window that opens at 7:55 a.m. PST (10:55 a.m. EST / 1555 UTC). Spaceflight Now will have live coverage beginning about 30 minutes prior to liftoff. SpaceX will launch the mission using the Falcon 9 first stage booster B1081, which is making its 29th launch. Its previous flights included NASA’s Crew-7, PACE, and TRACERS missions. Less than 8.5 minutes after liftoff, B1081 will target a landing on the droneship, Of Course I Still Love You , positioned in the Pacific Ocean. A successful recovery would mark the 236th landing on this vessel and the 681st booster landing to date. USSF-266 is the third in a series of missions using the ‘TH’ designation in public filings. Previous flights is this sequence were USSF-259/TH-1 on Sept. 16 and USSF-481/TH-2 on Oct. 15. Following each of those missions, 17 satellites were added into the orbital tracking catalogue maintained by the Space Force. While the Space Force declines to offer more information about these missions, it’s thought that these ‘TH’ missions are part of a $1.6 billion task order awarded to SpaceX for 18 Falcon 9 launches on behalf of the Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio. That award was announced back in late July by the Space Force’s Space Systems Command. This task order was established through the National Security Space Launch (NSSL) Phase 3 Lane 1 contract, which is designed to allow for a wide range of launch providers to bid on and receive task orders for payloads that can shoulder a higher risk tolerance.

historyItems.originalTitle: Arianespace launches 36 Amazon Leo sats amid rocket crunch
historyItems.originalSummary: An Ariane 64 rocket from Arianespace takes off from Europe's spaceport on the VA271/LE-04 mission for Amazon Leo on Nov. 24, 2026. Image: ESA-CNES-Arianespace-ArianeGroup / Optique video du CSG - P. Piron Update Nov. 24, 10:25 a.m. EST (1525 UTC): Arianespace successfully deployed all 36 satellites. Amazon Leo launched a batch of satellites onboard an Ariane 6 rocket Tuesday, nine days after it lost 40 satellites when United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket failed to reach orbit. Liftoff of the Leo Europe 4 (LE-04) mission from Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana happened at 8:14 a.m. Kourou Time (6:14 a.m. EST / 1114 UTC) at the end of the launch window. It was Amazon’s fourth flight on an Arianespace rocket and the tenth flight of the rocket overall. In April 2022, Amazon selected Arianespace to fly 18 missions for its constellation. That announcement also came with the choice of 38 Vulcan rocket launches and 12 onboard Blue Origin’s New Glenn rockets. The board of Amazon eventually pushed to add a trio of launches onboard SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets, all of which were flown in 2025. In late 2025, Amazon Leo also converted an option from Blue Origin to fly a total of 24 batches of satellites on New Glenn rockets. At the same time, the retail giant also purchased an additional 10 Falcon 9 rockets. However, both Blue Origin and ULA faced years of delays with the debuts of their heavy-lift launcher vehicles and suffered issues this year that significantly set back their launch capabilities. During ULA’s February launch of USSF-87, an anomaly with one of the Northrop Grumman-built GEM63 XL solid rocket motors caused Vulcan to be grounded for the majority of 2026. During its return-to-flight mission on Nov. 15, Vulcan suffered a different issue, this time with the rocket’s main booster. That caused the first full mission failure for ULA since its founding in 2006 and the loss of the 40 Amazon Leo satellites onboard. “There is risk with any launch, and that’s especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01,” Amazon said in a statement following the anomaly. “ULA has been a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they’ll learn from this mission and deliver on their long-term plans for Vulcan.” Meanwhile, Blue Origin’s fourth New Glenn rocket, intended for a launch of 48 Amazon Leo satellites, was destroyed along with some launch infrastructure during an explosion on the pad during a static fire test of the BE-4 engines. Amazon Leo’s satellites were not onboard the rocket when it blew up.

historyItems.originalTitle: HPE Lifts Outlook as AI Demand Boosts Revenue, Profit
historyItems.originalSummary: Server maker Hewlett-Packard Enterprise Co. posted its fastest quarterly revenue growth on record and raised its full-year forecast, but it wasn’t enough to keep up the momentum of a broader Nvidia Corp.-fueled rally, and its stock was headed lower after-hours. The company reported fourth-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of $1.43 per share, easily beating Wall Street’s target of $1.26 per share. Revenue for the period rose 50% from the same period one year earlier, to $14.55 billion, surpassing the Street’s $14.47 billion estimate. HPE also recorded a net profit of $1.82 billion, up from just $175 million in the year-ago period. The stunning revenue growth was a reflection of the enormous demand for artificial intelligence servers and networking equipment, said President and Chief Executive Antonio Neri (pictured). “Our record performance reflects the portfolio we have built to drive durable, profitable growth for our shareholders,” he said in a statement. HPE said it’s raising its revenue expectations for fiscal 2027, which ends next October, saying it’s now targeting growth of between 27% to 35%, or sales of between $59.4 billion and $63.1 billion. Previously, the company had been looking for growth of just 13% to 17%. Neri told analysts on a conference call that the updated guidance reflects the growing demand the company is seeing for AI servers that extends well into next year. He said the company has a strong position as the AI industry shifts from a focus on training models to supporting inference workloads and AI agents. “We have a perfect portfolio to capture that inflection point across networking, cloud and AI,” Neri said, citing “the durability of the demand and the durability of our execution now with a completely different setup in our portfolio.” According to Neri, the improved outlook also reflects the company’s view that the supply of key components such as memory, flash and networking equipment will remain constrained through to the end of calendar 2028. Despite the impressive forecast, HPE couldn’t sustain the momentum of an Nvidia-inspired rally that helped its stock jump more than 17% in regular trading before the earnings report. AI stocks in general received a huge boost earlier today on the news that the chipmaker has reinstated its founder and CEO Jensen Huang . But HPE fell more than 6% after-hours. For the current quarter, HPE is looking for revenue of between $14 billion and $14.6 billion, which would represent growth of 54% at the middle of that forecast. That suggests its revenue growth is going to accelerate and set a new company record. That forecast is strong too, with Wall Street analysts looking for first-quarter sales of just $13 billion. HPE’s biggest rival in the AI server business, Dell Technologies Inc., is expected to announce its own earnings results tomorrow afternoon, along with HP, Nutanix and Workday.

historyItems.originalTitle: Amazon to purchase Decart's AI optimization technology to advance chip and model innovation for customers
historyItems.originalSummary: Amazon announced it has signed an agreement to purchase the proprietary technology behind the Decart Optimization Stack, and bring the Decart AI co-founders – Dean Leitersdorf, Moshe Shalev, and Orian Leitersdorf – along with their team of AI researchers and engineers, to Amazon. "With their deep expertise in full-stack performance optimization across hardware and software, Decart brings a strong connection between technology and talent that will help further Amazon's investment in custom silicon and optimize AI inference for its customers. Amazon has long believed that inference speed and compute efficiency are central to the future of AI, and has advanced that vision through innovation across its custom silicon portfolio, from Graviton to Trainium. That work spans large language models, multimodal and agentic systems, and world models, alike. Amazon began working with Decart in 2025, and the collaboration quickly showed how much the two teams shared, from a full-stack view of performance to an appetite for solving some of the world's most challenging science and engineering problems," the company stated. "From day one, our mission has been to redefine the boundaries of what AI can do and to make it dramatically more efficient along the way. Joining Amazon gives our team the scale, the customers, and the infrastructure to pursue that mission faster than we could on our own. We're looking forward to exploring what we can build together," said Dean Leitersdorf, co-founder and CEO of Decart. Completion of the transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory clearance.

historyItems.originalTitle: Winter weather outlook: Will we see extreme snow and deep freezes again?
historyItems.originalSummary: A wet winter could be ahead for Mississippi, but will that mean rain, ice or snow ? NOAA's latest outlook offers new predictions for temperatures and precipitation this season. A record-strength El Niño is a factor in the forecast this year. It's already cut the Atlantic hurricane season short. And it might affect the polar vortex , which could cut down on cold snaps. "El Niño releases heat from the ocean and is expected to increase the risk of extreme heat, drought and heavy rainfall well into 2027," according to a World Meteorological Organization (WMO) news release issued earlier this month. This winter, El Niño could strengthen a storm track that will span the Southern U.S. Northern states, however, can look for a warm winter. AccuWeather , Old Farmer's Almanac , Farmers' Almanac and NOAA all expect different temperature ranges for the Gulf South, according to long-range forecasts. There is one thing all of them have in common: Mississippi should get some much-needed rain. Drought.gov says 97% of the state is currently in drought. Another 2% is abnormally dry. Whether increased precipitation means rain, ice or snow will depend on several factors. Blasts of arctic air from the polar vortex can cause deep cold fronts and freezing conditions, but how likely is that this year? Here's what the latest forecast tells us. Most of Mississippi has a high likelihood of near-normal temperatures, NOAA predicts. North Mississippi, however, has about a 33% to 40% chance of a warmer winter than usual from December through the end of February.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX launches intelligence-gathering satellites for the National Reconnaissance Office
historyItems.originalSummary: A Falcon 9 rocket stands poised to launch from the Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. File Photo: SpaceX Update Nov. 22, 8 a.m. EST (1300 UTC): SpaceX landed its booster at Landing Zone 4. SpaceX launched a batch of intelligence-gathering satellites to low Earth orbit on behalf of the National Reconnaissance Office on Sunday morning. Its Falcon 9 rocket took off from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, smashing the pad turnaround record at the site by more than 23 hours. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base is scheduled for 4:23 a.m. PST (7:23 a.m. EST / 1223 UTC). It came 32 hours, 3 minutes, and 21 seconds after the launch of the USSF. The previous turnaround was set back in June at 55 hours, 48 minutes, and 21 seconds. Prior to Sunday morning, SpaceX’s overall pad turnaround record was 45 hours, set by back-to-back Starlink flights from Cape Canaveral Space Force Base in Florida in January. The mission, designated NROL-136, will add an undisclosed number of satellites to the NRO’s satellite constellation that it refers to as its proliferated architecture. This was the fourth such launch this year and the 15th to date. SpaceX launched the mission using the Falcon 9 first stage booster with the tail number B1097. This was its 14th flight following the launches of NROL-172, USSF-259, Transporter-17, Twilight, Sentinel-6B, and eight batches of Starlink satellites. Roughly 7.5 minutes after liftoff, B1097 touched down at Landing Zone 4, adjacent to the launch pad. This was the 38th landing at this site and the 680th Falcon booster landing to date.

historyItems.originalTitle: I tested the Alexa Tablet 8 for a week. It’s Amazon’s best attempt at an iPad yet
historyItems.originalSummary: Testing the Amazon Alexa Tablet 8 felt like I was giving an ex a second chance because they fixed a couple of the character flaws that made me block their number in the first place. Amazon’s new tablets are shiny, metallic and feel premium, things you couldn’t say about the Fire tablets they replace. Even more importantly, Amazon finally fixed one of its biggest tablet sins that had always stopped them from being considered the best tablet in any category other than budget or for kids. So, how does the new entry-level Alexa Tablet 8 (and its bigger siblings) stack up against the Apple iPad 11? I spent the last few weeks digging into the new family of Amazon tablets to see how they compare to the king, and finding out who they’re actually for. Here’s what I learned. Amazon Alexa Tablet 8 Amazon’s replacement for the Fire tablets offers a stylish metallic design and actual Google Play Store support that finally brings YouTube and Chrome over. $230 From $130 at Amazon $230 From $150 at Best Buy What I liked about it Out of Fire’s ashes, colorful metallic shells offer a great design Having tested tablets for the better part of my 11-plus years writing tech product reviews, I’m happy to say that Amazon’s built one of the best-looking iPad clones I’ve ever seen. And I mean that as a compliment. Gone are the days of Amazon’s cheap, disposable plastic Fire tablets, replaced by shiny, metallic Alexa tablets, whose backs pick up the sunlight in delightful ways and exude the look of top Android tablets. From the bold colors — I really like the teal aluminum shell of my Alexa Tablet 8 — to their sturdy frames, these slates offer the best builds I’ve ever seen from Amazon’s Android tablet division. I prefer the color I tested, but Amazon also offers a Graphite black for those who like to blend into the crowd and a light purple Rosette design that I can’t knock either. Amazon finally accepts Google Play and real Android The Amazon Fire tablets’ biggest sin was one of omission, as they never had the Google Play Store and forced users to rely on Amazon’s own app ecosystem that didn’t have Gmail, YouTube and many other popular apps. This was the kind of mistake that had me saying very dismissive and unkind things about those tablets. Thankfully, Amazon’s reached the end of that error, which is great for everyone who wanted Chrome so they wouldn’t have to rely on Amazon’s slow and poorly designed Silk web browser. The Alexa Tablet 8 and its siblings run a very Alexa-infused version of Android 16 that promotes your own Amazon ecosystem content (such as Kindle e-books) in the top corner, and a whole “Ask Alexa” widget affixed to the bottom corner. While I was a bit hesitant about these integrations when I first started testing, I’ve come to see that they’re great ways to easily pick up where you left off in novels and shows or ask Alexa a quick question. As someone who is always reluctant to use voice assistants (especially their AI-based counterparts), I’m surprised that I’ve already found a place where Alexa+ impressed me. historyItems.title: SpaceX 為美國太空軍資料網路星座發射衛星
historyItems.summary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket flies away from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base on the USSF-317 mission on Nov. 20, 2026. Image: SpaceX Update Nov. 21: U.S.
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX launches satellites for the U.S. Space Force’s data network constellation
historyItems.originalSummary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket flies away from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base on the USSF-317 mission on Nov. 20, 2026. Image: SpaceX Update Nov. 21: U.S. Space Force confirmed the payload for the mission. SpaceX launched an undisclosed number of satellites on a Falcon 9 rocket on behalf of the U.S. Space Force on Friday night. SpaceX scrubbed the launch Thursday night, but didn’t state the reason why. The mission, designated USSF-317, flew from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 8:20 p.m. PST / 11:20 p.m. EST (0420 UTC on Saturday, Nov. 21). The rocket took off on a south-easterly trajectory upon leaving the pad. Following deployment, the government issued a short statement, confirming publicly for the first time the intention of a series of missions launched this year that have received an ‘R’ designation in public filings. “With three successful launches in two weeks, the Department of the Air Force is accelerating the development and launch of the Space Data Network Backbone constellation, advancing a government-owned and controlled communication system that will provide secure, high-speed data transport globally for the Joint Force,” said the Secretary of the Air Force Public Affairs in a press release. “The accelerated schedule is on track to deliver regional capability this year and global support by next year.” The Space Data Network (SDN) Backbone comes from the Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) of the Space-Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST), an acquisition office within the Space Force. Back in May, the Space Force announced its award of a $2.29 billion contract to SpaceX to build a satellite constellation that “functions as an integrated network, providing robust, resilient, high-capacity, and low-latency data transport for the Joint Force.” The Space Force said back in May that the SDN Backbone would operate alongside the Space Development Agency’s Transport Layer, a constellation of data relaying satellites manufactured by Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, and York Space Systems. historyItems.originalTitle: The Best CRM Software We've Tested for 2026
historyItems.originalSummary: You need to pay attention not only to customer information originating in the CRM but also to supporting data from other systems, such as your customer support software . You can't reliably communicate with customers if your data is inaccurate or disorganized, which means lost revenue. Ensuring good data quality is a matter of testing and constant vigilance. Depending on the size of your staff, you might need to hire someone to manage all data management tasks, including automating workflows, backup , and protection. If you feel such a hire is in your future, involve that person in your CRM search as early as possible. When you work with customer data, security should be top of mind. It's a warning sign when your CRM doesn't generate an audit trail whenever someone changes a password, or if it doesn't let you define access controls for each user. Customer data is extremely valuable, especially now that customers are more reluctant to part with it. Securing it isn't just about maintaining privacy; it's about protecting profitable relationships. You should ensure that your CRM software integrates with as much of your current IT security stack as possible, including your identity management system, so your employees can use single sign-on (SSO) or multi-factor authentication . But you also need to closely evaluate a vendor's policies to ascertain exactly where your data resides, who is responsible for its safety, and what happens if there's a problem. Search for any past breaches and how the company responded to them as well.

historyItems.originalTitle: The first Nvidia RTX Spark mini PCs launch today from Asus, Dell, and MSI
historyItems.originalSummary: After the first RTX Spark laptops launched earlier this year, Nvidia’s RTX Spark N1X chip is also now available in desktops from Asus, Dell, and MSI . More RTX Spark desktops are coming later from Acer, Gigabyte, and HP, while Microsoft’s Surface RTX Spark Dev Box is slated to start shipping this month. The new mini PCs include a 6144-core Nvidia Blackwell RTX GPU, 20-core Nvidia Grace CPU, and up to 128GB of memory. That high-end hardware comes with a price to match — Asus’s ProArt GR1X starts at $4,499 for a configuration with 64GB of memory and 1TB of storage. Like the RTX Spark laptops that compete with the MacBook Pro and the DGX Spark desktop Nvidia launched last year, the new mini PCs are Mac Mini or Mac Studio alternatives for developers working with local AI models, as well as RTX-accelerated software. That includes the AI-powered features for tools like Adobe Premiere and Photoshop, and new DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support in Blender 5.3. They can run games too , and Windows on Arm game support is improving, but at these prices, that’s not a realistic reason to pick one up yet. Nvidia says they can act as a “dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents,” and deliver “up to 1 petaflop of AI performance.” They also feature native CUDA support and access to Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux.

historyItems.originalTitle: Project Gryffindor: Meta's plan to get more school kids using Instagram
historyItems.originalSummary: Internal Meta documents show the company planned to boost Instagram use among teens by targeting schools in an initiative it named "Project Gryffindor." The project focused on growing what it called "school communities" in the U.S. by encouraging teens to include their school banner on their profiles and establishing a student directory that allows users to see and connect with others from their school who use the platform. Meta launched the initiative in 2025, calling it a "school partnership program," and significantly expanded it in September 2026. The company said almost 17,000 schools had signed up for the program at the time. Meta said the program sought to provide a safer experience on Instagram for children, including protecting them from bullying and online risks by allowing educators to report safety concerns to the company. Another feature gives school-related accounts the ability to post stories and notes visible to all verified students and parents in a school community. Meta said these features would help students and parents stay informed about happenings at school. The announcement gave an example of a school using the Instagram Stories feature to share a notice of basketball tryouts. However, in internal documents prior to the program's public launch, the company discussed more explicitly commercial motivations for establishing school networks. In a 2024 presentation on Project Gryffindor, Meta said that embedding in schools was a way to increase user "acquisition," "friending" and "invites" to join Instagram. Gryffindor is one of the four Hogwarts school houses from the Harry Potter books. "We believe network connections will fuel organic and unattributed acquisition," the project's presentation states, referring to adding new users. "Our current strategy of relying on power user teens to get less active friends onto IG may not be effective if there are full communities of teens that have not yet joined IG," the presentation stated. The previously unreported Meta documents are part of evidence obtained by lawyers through discovery in a multidistrict lawsuit alleging that social media platforms are designed to be harmful to users under 18, and that the companies knew their products carried risks they failed to disclose. Meta, alongside TikTok, Google and Snap, are defendants in the cases, which were brought by children and their families, school districts and state attorneys general.

historyItems.originalTitle: NASA to Cover 35th SpaceX Resupply Mission Space Station Departure
historyItems.originalSummary: NASA is preparing to broadcast the departure of a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft from the International Space Station (ISS). The spacecraft is set to return to Earth no earlier than Wednesday, November 18, after completing its 35th resupply mission. It will carry research samples, equipment, and other cargo back from the station. According to NASA, Dragon is scheduled to undock from the space-facing port of the station’s Harmony module at 11:05 a.m. EST, depending on weather conditions. Ground controllers at SpaceX’s facility in Hawthorne, California, will send the command for the spacecraft to leave. NASA’s live coverage will begin at 10:45 a.m. EST. People can watch the event through the agency’s website and other streaming platforms. The full details are available on NASA’s live coverage page. SpaceX Dragon prepares to return to Earth After 34 days docked to the @Space_Station, the Dragon spacecraft supporting SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission for @NASA is targeted to undock from the orbiting lab as soon as Wednesday, November 18 → https://t.co/tnMukzSxui https://t.co/OhkzWO1fRh — SpaceX (@SpaceX) November 17, 2026 NASA and SpaceX are watching weather conditions around the planned splashdown area off the California coast. The spacecraft is expected to reach the ocean no earlier than 1:50 a.m. EST on Thursday, November 19. This is 10:50 p.m. PST on Wednesday, November 18. The return schedule may change depending on weather conditions in the recovery area. NASA said it would share updates about the splashdown time on its space station blog. The agency will not provide a live broadcast of the splashdown. Research samples and equipment returning from space The spacecraft will be returning with many kilograms of scientific samples to help scientists on Earth and in space. A 3D printed blood vessel sample was studied to understand age-related disease of blood vessels and the heart. Frozen tumour organoids have also been treated on the station and will be returned to Earth to investigate how cancer treatments can be improved. Microbes, which have been frozen, will be returned to Earth to give scientists insight into how antibiotic resistant bacteria adapt and change in space. Finally, a lighting system which has been on the station for over 3 years will be returned. It was tested to see if it could assist astronauts to get better quality sleep and maintain good health during long missions. A mission that delivered more than 6,300 pounds of cargo A Dragon spacecraft carrying over 6,300 pounds of supplies, scientific experiments and equipment docked with the station on October 15. The craft was carried into space by a Falcon 9 rocket on October 13 from Florida as the 35th resupply mission for NASA and SpaceX. Experiments conducted on the International Space Station, which has been occupied by astronauts for over 26 years, are helping prepare for future missions to the Moon and Mars.

historyItems.originalTitle: Microsoft and Salesforce Announce Copilotforce, Bringing Trusted Customer Context and Action into Microsoft AI Experiences
historyItems.originalSummary: REDMOND, Wash., and SAN FRANCISCO — Nov. 17, 2026 — Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ: MSFT) and Salesforce Inc. (NYSE: CRM) today announced Copilotforce, a new partnership that helps employees get more done in the tools they already use by bringing Salesforce customer context, business processes and actions into Microsoft Copilot and other AI-powered productivity experiences. Unveiled at Microsoft Ignite, the partnership introduces new integrations across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Fabric, including Salesforce in Copilot, a plugin available in public preview with 38+ prebuilt sales skills. Together, these capabilities help businesses move faster, reduce manual work and get more value from their existing technology investments — while maintaining the security, governance and permissions they already rely on. Bringing Salesforce workflows together with conversations, meetings and documents in Microsoft 365 means less time spent moving between systems and more time on the work that matters. Salesforce in Copilot connects customer context with the work happening across the business so employees can make more informed decisions and take action without constantly switching applications. Microsoft Work IQ, the intelligence layer powering Copilot, provides relevant context from Teams meetings, Outlook emails and documents across SharePoint and OneDrive. Work IQ and Salesforce help sellers understand not only what’s recorded in CRM, but what’s happening across customer conversations and collaboration — and what needs to happen next. Through authenticated Salesforce MCP access, sellers can securely retrieve customer information and take supported business actions within their existing Salesforce permissions. Salesforce continues to govern access and business actions, while Microsoft applies its existing enterprise compliance controls to communications and documents. Data, context and the apps where sellers work come to life in practical workflows across the sales cycle, including: With Copilot as the front door to business process, Salesforce in Copilot allows organizations to bring together Salesforce data, workflows, agents and prebuilt skills from the systems they already rely on through Copilot’s open and interoperable platform. “Through Copilotforce, we’re bringing Salesforce to the largest surface in enterprise software today, embedding trusted Salesforce context and intelligent sales workflows directly where sellers work,” said Miguel Milano, President & Chief Operating Officer, Salesforce . “By bringing together the #1 CRM with the #1 productivity surface, we’re transforming AI from a standalone tool into a powerful driver of productivity, smarter decisions and customer success.” Expanding connection in the places people work For many organizations, the work first starts in Microsoft Teams, where people share files, make decisions and hand work to each other. historyItems.originalTitle: Why Vertiv’s Big AI Data Center Power Breakthrough Couldn’t Save the Stock Today
historyItems.originalSummary: Vertiv has widened its 800 VDC power range for AI data centres from the rack to two further levels. On 25 November 2026 the company added systems for the compute pod and the data hall, building on the Vertiv PowerDirect 5000 Power Rack it introduced in May 2026. The company says operators are weighing 800 VDC as a route to higher-density computing, but that AC and DC architectures will coexist and adoption will not follow a single timeline. Its approach is to let operators bring 800 VDC in at different points of the power train without committing a whole facility to one design. At rack level, the PowerDirect 5000 (±400 or 800 VDC) sits beside the IT rack, configurable up to 800 kW. It takes facility 480 VAC, holds 30 hot-pluggable 30 kW power supply units and includes a battery backup unit designed to give at least 50 seconds of hold-up time. Inside the compute rack, the PowerDirect 3000 power shelf converts 800 VDC to 54 VDC at up to 98.5% peak efficiency. Moving conversion outside the rack frees 8 to 16 rack units for compute, and operators can keep their existing upstream AC infrastructure. For a whole row or pod, the PowerDirect 9000 Power Center converts 480 VAC to 800 VDC at 1.5 MW, scaling in 60 kW steps across 27 hot-pluggable supply units. It feeds the PowerBar Track DC busway, and an EnergyCore Li5 800 VDC battery cabinet connects directly to the DC bus with 200 kW of continuous backup; up to six cabinets can run in parallel. At data hall scale, the PowerNexus MV SST is a 5 MW solid-state transformer that converts medium-voltage AC straight to 800 VDC in one stage, removing two to three intermediate conversion steps. Outdoor, liquid-cooled and containerised, it is rated at up to 98% AC-to-DC efficiency and can support a 4.8 MW super pod reference architecture without chaining. Vertiv also lists touch-proof busbars, high-voltage isolation, midpoint grounding, ground-fault detection and arc-flash prevention among the safety features of the DC designs. Pilot programmes, technical validation and joint development with customers are under way. Scott Armul, Chief Product and Technology Officer at Vertiv, said: "The 800 VDC power train is not just a new power product or conversion methodology; it is a set of architectures and system designs." Kyle Keeper, Senior Vice President of Vertiv's Power Management Business Unit, added: "Different operators have different requirements, whether they’re building new AI facilities, upgrading existing sites, or supporting a mix of tenants and workloads." historyItems.originalTitle: Doug's 2026-27 Winter Weather Outlook: How much snow will the DC area get?
historyItems.originalSummary: As a beautiful fall winds down, FOX 5 NY's Nick Gregory is sharing his 2026-2027 winter outlook, which is shaping up to be a lot milder than last season, when nearly 60 inches of snow fell in New York City. JUMP TO: FIRST DAY OF WINTER l ‘SUPER EL NIÑO’ l SNOW TOTAL PREDICTIONSWinter forecasts this year come down to four key indicators: Winter officially begins in the Northern Hemisphere on Dec. 21 with the winter solstice – the day with the least amount of possible daylight and the longest night.El Niño refers to warmer-than-average sea surface temperatures along the equatorial latitude in the Pacific Ocean.It causes an intensified southern jet stream that forces the polar jet stream to retreat further into southern Canada. The results are milder, dry conditions in the northern U.S. and a cool, wetter-than-normal forecast for the southern part of the country.This year, we're experiencing a "Super El Niño," with water temperatures rising to a historic 4.77°F above average, outpacing each of the four previous "Super El Niño" years of 2015, 1997, 1982 and 1877. A strong El Niño winter doesn't automatically mean there won't be snow. It tends to bring more coastal storms along the Eastern Seaboard, but the above-average temperatures mean rain is more likely.El Niño can still cause a variety of outcomes. In 2015-2016, the region saw a total of 31.2" of snow, but 27.5" came from one blockbuster storm in January 2016.Here are the other previous totals:Gregory describes the polar vortex as a high-speed "racetrack wind pattern" that circles the North Pole when stable. If it becomes fractured or weakened, arctic air can spill down into the eastern U.S. The polar vortex weakened in early November this year, which has never happened for as long as forecasters have been tracking it. This is worth keeping an eye on. The North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) is a pressure oscillation that stretches from the North Atlantic down to the subtropical Atlantic.When in its negative phase, the NAO forms a blocking pattern around Greenland that forces cold air down from Canada, resulting in coastal storms. In the past, this has caused some major snowstorms in the New York City area. In its positive phase, the NAO sees much stronger pressure variation in the Atlantic, resulting in a stronger westerly wind. Cold air stays north, keeping temperatures mild around here. Arctic, or Siberian, snow cover started early this year. In fact, it's already above average. What does that mean? Colder air can more easily travel across the North Pole, disrupt the polar vortex and send more cold air into the eastern U.S. Gregory predicts there will be multiple coastal storms this winter, but with a lower-than-average amount of snow. Since the super El Niño leads to milder temperatures, the storms can vary between snow, ice and rain along the coast. You'll probably have to be well inland to get a good amount of snow this year.Gregory predicts New York City and the nearby suburbs could see 12-20" of snow this year, but he notes that might be too generous, all things considered. historyItems.originalTitle: FAA Air Traffic Ground Stop Investigation: HPE Juniper Routers, Cisco Routers, And The Aftermath Of A Telecom Network Upgrade
historyItems.originalSummary: Here’s a look at how a telecom network upgrade involving a move from 20-year-old Cisco routers to modern HPE Juniper routers led to the nationwide air traffic ground stop last Friday. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) nationwide air traffic ground stop last Friday, which resulted from a telecom network upgrade involving a move from 20-year-old Cisco routers to modern HPE Juniper routers, is now zeroing in on older Cisco equipment, said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in an interview on CNBC. “What happened was as we did one of those switchovers in El Dorado, Ark., that server or that router started to flood our network,” said Duffy Monday of the network upgrade from old copper wires to fiber. “Well, all of the work I had done to put in new equipment, those routers in my system didn’t go down. But we also use a lot of 2001 Cisco servers that went out of commission in 2006. It is those old servers that were flooded and started to give us inconsistency in our network.” At this point, Duffy said, the Cisco server in question has been taken to federal contractor and technology solution provider L3Harris Technologies’ Florida laboratory as part of an investigation into the incident with FAA staff on site. CRN reached out to Cisco for comment but had not heard back at press time. As a result of the network issue, Duffy said the decision was made to “shut down the airspace” until the U.S. could “isolate where the flooding of the network was coming from, remedy it, get the systems working again and get air travel back to normal,” said Duffy. In a press conference on Saturday, Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford told reporters that the FAA spends a billion dollars a year maintaining and sustaining its 1980s TDMI telco network, which he referred to as a 1G system. “We are constantly replacing 2,000 Cisco 600 routers with Juniper routers,” he said. “So, this is ordinary course-of-business stuff.” Those Cisco 600 routers were manufactured between 2001 and 2006. The upgrade from Cisco routers to HPE Juniper equipment was being conducted by Melbourne, Fla.-based L3Harris, which is under contract with the U.S. government, runs the telecom network. L3Harris, which has been working with the FAA for over 20 years, is now under scrutiny on whether there was a misconfiguration issue with regard to the HPE Juniper router as part of the network upgrade.

historyItems.originalTitle: Elon Musk Wants to Merge Tesla and SpaceX. Their Businesses Already Overlap.
historyItems.originalSummary: Thank you for your patience while we verify access. Nearly a decade ago, Elon Musk gave Tesla’s design team an unusual assignment: Build a sports car that can fly. Mr. Musk brought in a small team of engineers from SpaceX, his rocket company, to lend a hand. Led by Bill Riley, SpaceX’s executive overseeing engineering on the rocket intended to land NASA astronauts on the moon, the team juggled their day jobs with outfitting a Roadster sports car with cold-gas thrusters, a technology more commonly found in rockets that has enough force to burst a human eardrum, according to three people familiar with the project. This year, as engineers from both companies prepared for the car’s debut, they spent months putting it through its paces at SpaceX’s rocket testing facility in McGregor, Texas, the people said. In October, a driverless Roadster did a kick flip in midair, launching off a ramp more than 60 feet high. This is “what happens when you have a collaboration with the world’s best car company and the world’s best rocket company” Mr. Musk told the crowd.

historyItems.originalTitle: Nebius Lowers Outlook, Addresses Worries Over Financing AI Buildout
historyItems.originalSummary: By Kelly Cloonan Nebius Group lowered its full-year revenue outlook, citing a delay in some third-party capacity. The artificial-intelligence cloud company also addressed recent concerns over financing its buildout, emphasizing its momentum with customer prepayments. Nebius said Thursday it now expects full-year revenue to come in at the low end of its prior guidance range of $3 billion to $3.4 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet are forecasting $3.35 billion. The updated guidance factors in a portion of this year's revenue moving into next year, with some third-party capacity Nebius had expected to come online this year now scheduled for the first half of 2027, the company said. The contracts behind that capacity remain in place, the company said. Nebius also gave an initial outlook for next year, guiding for revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, compared with analyst projections of $12.09 billion. The company said the forecast reflects a conservative approach to the pace of its buildout, and that it continues to expect to bring online more than 1 gigawatt of new capacity each year. "Our focus remains on building a healthy, profitable business for the long term," Chief Executive Arkady Volozh said in a letter to shareholders. The guidance comes amid investor worries over how neocloud companies will finance their growing footprints. CoreWeave, whose borrowing costs have surged in recent weeks and helped spark the market jitters, eased some of those concerns earlier this week after reporting better-than-expected quarterly revenue. Volozh said Nebius is able to finance its buildout in a prudent way through customer prepayments and a healthy balance sheet, helped by a strategy that lets it command premium prices and terms, and bring down its costs of infrastructure from designing and building it itself. Nebius expects prepayments and financing against existing contracts with investment-grade customers to cover 75% to 85% of its capital expenditures in 2027, and has a wide range of other funding options available, Volozh said. "Our confidence in the fundamentals of what we are building has not changed, and the opportunity ahead of us is as large as it has ever been. We will keep going," Volozh said. Nebius shares slid 12% to $136.66 in premarket trading. Nebius reported a third-quarter loss of $37.5 million, or 13 cents a share, compared with a loss of $119.6 million, or 50 cents a share, a year earlier. Revenue surged by more than six-fold to $980.8 million, compared with analyst estimates of $907.2 million. Write to Kelly Cloonan at kelly.cloonan@wsj.com (END) Dow Jones Newswires 11-12-26 0838ET

historyItems.originalSummary: Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL), a leader in data infrastructure semiconductor solutions and Penguin Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: PENG), the AI Factory Platform Company, today announced a strategic collaboration to address AI memory demands. This collaboration brings together two complementary technologies: CXL-based memory expansion that enables data centers to extend server memory capacity using existing DDR4 memory, and advanced photonic technology designed to enable high-bandwidth, low latency memory sharing across multiple racks.As AI workloads shift from model training to large-scale inference and agentic AI, memory capacity, bandwidth, and latency are becoming critical constraints on application performance and token economics. Growing model sizes, longer context windows, and expanding KV-cache requirements are driving memory needs into hundreds of gigabytes and increasingly terabytes per node. These demands are accelerating the shift beyond traditional server-attached memory toward memory expansion, pooling, and disaggregation technologies such as CXL and optical shared-memory fabrics, enabling memory capacity to scale independently of compute.Two Complementary Levels of Memory ExpansionMarvell and Penguin Solutions are developing two complementary memory expansion technologies designed to address AI infrastructure needs at the server and pod levels:Direct-attach memory expansion: The planned addition of Marvell® Structera™ X memory-expansion controllers within Penguin Solutions SMART® CXL AICs enables data centers to unlock additional memory capacity by recycling existing high-density DDR4 memory modules from decommissioned servers and connecting them directly to servers through PCIe 5.0 and CXL 2.0. This approach provides scalable, low-latency memory expansion in a standard form factor designed for broader industry adoption.Multi-rack photonic memory pooling: By integrating Marvell® Photonic Fabric™ optical interconnect technology-based memory modules and NICs into Penguin Solutions MemoryAI™ memory appliances and ComputeAI™ systems, AI data centers will be able to support low-latency, high-bandwidth, multi-rack disaggregated memory sharing across longer distances, enabling petabyte-scale memory pools for context-rich agentic AI inference.These two technologies are highly complementary. Direct-attach memory expansion addresses immediate, server-level capacity needs today, while multi-rack photonic memory sharing is designed to enable high-bandwidth, low-latency memory sharing across multiple racks to support increasingly demanding AI workloads. historyItems.title: SK 海力士計畫設立晶片測試中心以推動韓國小型企業的發展
historyItems.summary: SK HYNIX plans to open a semiconductor testing facility in 2027 in partnership with the South Korean government, angling to boost the global competitiveness of the country’s smaller chip equipment makers. The 874.6 billion won (US$654 million) facility is being built inside the sprawling Yongin Semiconductor Cluster, which is under construction south of Seoul, SK Hynix said in a statement on Monday (Nov 16). The Trinity Fab facility will open in May with equipment that small and medium-sized suppliers can use to conduct final performance and yield validation before their products are deployed in commercial chipmaking lines, it said.

historyItems.originalTitle: ULA suffers first outright failure with loss of Vulcan rocket carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
historyItems.originalSummary: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan, equipped with six solid rocket boosters, lifts off from Cape Canaveral's pad 41. A failure 10 minutes into flight resulted in the loss of 40 Amazon Leo satellites. Image: Michael Cain/Spaceflight Now In a major setback for United Launch Alliance, the company’s new heavy-lift Vulcan rocket carrying a batch of Amazon Leo internet satellites, malfunctioned during the climb to space Sunday, dooming the payload and throwing a costly wrench into the launch schedule of both companies. “Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 (at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station) suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit,” ULA said in a statement some 50 minutes after liftoff. “We will work closely with our customer and other appropriate organizations to find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action and return to flight as quickly as possible.” It was the first outright failure of a United Launch Alliance rocket since the company, a partnership between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, was formed in 2006. It wasn’t immediately known what went wrong, but the Vulcan, the rocket replacing ULA’s fleet of Atlas 5 rockets, will face a potentially significant grounding while engineers review telemetry and implement fixes for whatever caused the mishap. It was only the fifth flight of a Vulcan rocket and the first in nine months as ULA and booster-supplier Northrop Grumman worked to resolve problems with nozzles used by strap-on solid-fuel boosters that marred two earlier flights. The solids appeared to work normally Sunday, helping boost the rocket out of the dense lower atmosphere before burning out and falling away. The two methane-burning BE-4 engines powering the Vulcan’s first stage then continued the climb toward orbit, but they appeared to fire longer than expected based on ULA’s pre-launch timeline. After stage separation, the Vulcan’s hydrogen-fueled Centaur upper stage engines took over for a planned 12-minute 15-second burn. According to ULA’s update, something went wrong during that Centaur firing, but no additional details were immediately provided. Sunday’s launch was the first of 38 Vulcan flights purchased by Amazon to launch its Leo satellites, designed to compete head-to-head with Elon Musk’s Starlinks and other space-based internet providers. ULA already has launched eight LEO flights using Atlas 5 rockets.

Firefly will supply the propulsion technology while maintaining ownership of its underlying intellectual property. AST SpaceMobile will receive a license allowing it to manufacture the engines for its launch program.

historyItems.title: SpaceX 歷史性首次捕捉 Starship 火箭上級
historyItems.summary: SpaceX has achieved a major milestone in its Starship programme by successfully catching the rocket's upper stage using giant mechanical arms attached to its launch tower. The spacecraft returned to Earth after spending 22.5 hours in space, marking the first successful recovery of the Ship through this technique. However, the mission was only partially successful, as the rocket's lower section failed its planned recovery attempt. Starship completes 22.5-hour flight The 124-metre-tall Starship rocket lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase launch facility in Boca Chica, Texas, at 16:47 local time on Friday.
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX has achieved a major milestone in its Starship programme by successfully catching the rocket's upper stage using giant mechanical arms attached to its launch tower. The spacecraft returned to Earth after spending 22.5 hours in space, marking the first successful recovery of the Ship through this technique. However, the mission was only partially successful, as the rocket's lower section failed its planned recovery attempt. Starship completes 22.5-hour flight The 124-metre-tall Starship rocket lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase launch facility in Boca Chica, Texas, at 16:47 local time on Friday. This was the 15th test flight of the spacecraft and the first attempt to recover both sections of the rocket during the same mission. After reaching space, the upper stage, known as the Ship, deployed 26 satellites for SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation. It subsequently completed 14 orbits around Earth before beginning its return journey. The moment a Starship booster exploded during an attempted landing at SpaceX’s facility today. https://t.co/HoRscWHVH0 — распад и неуважение (@VictorKvert2008) November 14, 2026 &nbsp; How did SpaceX catch Starship? As the Ship approached its launch site, it hovered near the launch tower, where two enormous mechanical arms, nicknamed 'chopsticks', moved into position and secured the returning spacecraft. The arms are part of SpaceX's Mechazilla recovery system, which is designed to catch returning rocket stages instead of allowing them to land on the ground using conventional landing legs. This was the first time SpaceX successfully caught Starship's upper stage. The company had previously demonstrated the technique with its Super Heavy booster, which it had caught on three earlier test flights. What happened to Starship's booster? While the upper-stage recovery succeeded, the mission encountered a problem during the attempted recovery of the Super Heavy booster. The lower section was expected to return to the launch tower approximately six and a half minutes after liftoff. However, an automated abort system cancelled the catch attempt and diverted the booster towards the ocean. The booster hovered above the water before bursting into flames. Elon Musk later said on X that it was "slightly low on fuel". Why does SpaceX want to recover both stages? SpaceX aims to make Starship completely reusable to reduce the cost of launching payloads into space. Recovering both sections would allow the company to inspect, refuel and prepare the rocket for subsequent flights. The approach builds on the company's Falcon 9 programme, whose reusable boosters have helped reduce launch costs. Why is this important for NASA's Moon mission? Starship's development is closely linked to NASA's Artemis programme. SpaceX has a contract to develop a lunar lander based on Starship that could transport astronauts to the Moon's surface. However, the company must demonstrate reliable recovery and repeated operations before Starship can fulfil its ambitious role in future lunar missions.
